goal: Understand SQL window functions well enough to rewrite my self-join reports
interpretation: After 30 minutes of watching, the learner can read and write PostgreSQL window functions (OVER, PARTITION BY, ranking, LAG/LEAD, running totals) and confidently replace their self-join based reports with them.
assumptions: Self-join reports are typically things like previous-row comparisons, running totals, and top-N per group, so the plan targets those patterns.
'No full SQL courses' means the learner wants short, focused videos rather than long multi-hour course uploads.
PostgreSQL syntax is preferred, but examples in other SQL dialects are acceptable since window function syntax is largely standard.

sub_topics.title: OVER() and PARTITION BY: how window functions differ from GROUP BY
sub_topics.why: The learner knows GROUP BY aggregates well, so the key shift is keeping row-level detail while computing per-group values.

sub_topics.title: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK with ORDER BY inside OVER
sub_topics.why: Replaces self-joins and correlated subqueries used for top-N per group and de-duplication.

sub_topics.title: LAG and LEAD for previous/next row comparisons
sub_topics.why: Self-joins on id-1 or date-1 for period-over-period reports are exactly what LAG/LEAD replace.

sub_topics.title: Running totals and window frames (ROWS BETWEEN, default frame behavior)
sub_topics.why: Cumulative sums and moving averages are usually done with self-joins on <= conditions; frames make this simple and fast.

sub_topics.title: Rewriting self-join reports with window functions in PostgreSQL
sub_topics.why: Ties the pieces together by converting real self-join queries into window function versions, which is the learner's actual goal.

picks.title: SQL Window Functions | Clearly Explained | PARTITION BY, ORDER BY, ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK
picks.reason: A step-by-step PostgreSQL walkthrough of OVER, ORDER BY, ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK and PARTITION BY on a small table. It ends with filtering window results in a subquery, which is the top-N-per-group pattern that self-joins usually handle. It skips LAG/LEAD and frames, so those are covered by other picks.

evidence.quote: SQL Pocket Guide author Alice Zhao breaks down each part of a window function, step-by-step.

picks.confidence_note: Based on the chapter list and description only, with no transcript. The chapters match the sub-topics well and the video is short and uses PostgreSQL. Confidence would rise with a transcript showing the examples.

picks.title: SQL LAG and LEAD Functions: Compare Rows & Month-over-Month Change
picks.reason: A short lesson on comparing each row with the previous or next row for period-over-period change. This is the main job self-joins do in reports, and it is the quickest way to learn LAG/LEAD. The examples use SQLite, but the syntax is the same in PostgreSQL.

evidence.quote: Compare each row with the previous or next row and calculate period-over-period changes.
Every example runs real SQL on SQLite, with the code on the left and the result on the right.

picks.confidence_note: Based on the description only, so the depth is unknown at 3.8 minutes. It uses SQLite rather than PostgreSQL. A transcript showing PARTITION BY with LAG would raise confidence.

picks.title: SQL Window Frames Explained! 🔥 | ROWS BETWEEN, PRECEDING & CURRENT ROW | Real SQL Problem
picks.reason: Covers window frames (ROWS BETWEEN, PRECEDING, CURRENT ROW) and a rolling SUM, solved as a practical problem in PostgreSQL. This is the running-total and rolling-window pattern that self-join reports often build by hand.

evidence.quote: In this tutorial, we'll explore how SQL Window Frames work and how to use them to calculate rolling totals and analyze data over a specific set of rows.
Calculating Rolling SUM using Window Frames

picks.confidence_note: Based on the description and chapter list only. It is PostgreSQL and practical, but it is unclear whether it explains the default frame behaviour of ORDER BY inside OVER.

picks.title: How to Use Window Functions for High-Performance Postgres Queries
picks.reason: A short PostgreSQL overview of GROUP BY versus window functions and ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LEAD and LAG. It promises to replace self-joins with windowed operations, which is the only candidate aimed at this goal. Watch it last as a capstone that ties the earlier pieces to rewriting reports.

evidence.quote: We’ll show you how to identify bottlenecks in your current SQL and replace them with high-performance windowed operations.
The difference between GROUP BY and window functions. How to use essential window functions like ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), LEAD(), and LAG().

picks.confidence_note: Based on the description only, and at 5.8 minutes the self-join rewrite is likely shallow. It is the only candidate that targets this sub-topic, so it fills the slot despite thin evidence.
